__baseline_prompt__.text: A photographic moment of cosmic horror, with human scale overwhelmed by an incomprehensible nonhuman presence. Use the supplied portrait as face-and-hair appearance guidance: a woman with a soft oval face, large brown eyes and natural pink lips, and a glossy dark chin-length bob with airy bangs. Her clothing and body are designed for this scene. She has stopped a small empty freight trolley one step short of the open elevator in an old municipal service corridor. She stands on the corridor floor outside the threshold, her right hand resting around the trolley handle, her elbow close to her side. Her face is in a readable three-quarter view, eyes fixed past the doorway; her lips have parted before a breath, while the trolley has stopped squarely against her thigh. Her dark knit sleeveless top, bare neck and softly lit cheek give her a quiet, personal presence against the mechanical surroundings. This is an encounter with an alien order that does not acknowledge its human observer. Beyond the worn steel doorframe, one continuous pearl-grey organism fills an immense living interior. Upright ribbed membranes separate into successive fan-shaped chambers around a common black opening. Translucent branching vessels cross the smooth membranes. The nearest membrane is taller than the elevator doors; the same connected body repeats into a depth the narrow shaft cannot contain. Its folds run through the expected floor and rear wall as if the small building were only a thin cut across its scale. The woman faces a presence whose visible extent defeats the familiar room, caught in the instant when a routine trip has become impossible to continue. Photograph from the corridor, at chest height with a restrained 35 mm perspective, looking diagonally across the woman's front-left side toward the open doors. A horizontal frame holds her from mid-thigh upward in the near left third, with her face large enough to recognize and the complete doorframe and receding membranes occupying the right two-thirds. Warm, worn corridor light falls over her face and trolley; a cold diffuse glow comes through the creature's layered tissue. Keep both the near human features and first several layers of the organism legible, allowing the far repetition to recede into darkness. Real steel scuffs, dust at the sill, ordinary knit texture and natural skin render this impossible event as an observed photograph. The central contrast is her small halted practical gesture against the vast indifferent continuity beyond the door.
